name: cbind.zoo
title: Merge Two or More zoo Objects

origin.usage: cbind.zoo(..., all = TRUE, fill = NA, suffixes = NULL, drop = FALSE, sep = ".")

arguments.text: Series to bind, passed to merge.zoo.

arguments.name: all
arguments.text: Logical vector recycled to the number of series. TRUE keeps that series' index.

arguments.name: suffixes
arguments.text: Names used to build column names.

arguments.name: drop
arguments.text: FALSE, so a single series stays a one-column matrix.

arguments.name: sep
arguments.text: Separator pasted between a suffix and a column name.

origin.details: cbind.zoo calls merge.zoo with retclass "zoo" and drop FALSE. all = FALSE keeps the indexes present in every series.
origin.example:
x <- zoo(c(1, 3, 5), c(1, 2, 4))
y <- zoo(c(2, 4, 6), c(2, 3, 4))
z <- cbind(x, y, all = FALSE)
show <- function(v) paste(vapply(as.numeric(v), function(a) if (is.na(a)) "NA" else sprintf("%.16g", a), ""), collapse = " ")
cat(show(coredata(z)), "\n", sep = "")
cat(show(index(z)), "\n", sep = "")

translation.usage: cbind_zoo(*args, all=True, fill=nan, suffixes=None, drop=False, sep=".")

arguments.name: *args
arguments.text: Series to bind, passed to merge_zoo.

arguments.name: all
arguments.text: Logical vector recycled to the number of series. True keeps that series' index.

arguments.name: suffixes
arguments.text: Names used to build column names. When omitted, the names are X1, X2, and so on.

arguments.name: drop
arguments.text: False, so a single series stays a one-column matrix.

arguments.name: sep
arguments.text: Separator pasted between a suffix and a column name.

translation.details: cbind_zoo calls merge_zoo with retclass "zoo" and drop False. all=False keeps the indexes present in every series. A matrix is Fortran order.
translation.example:
import math
import numpy as np
from zoo.series import Zoo
from zoo.merge import cbind_zoo

def show(values):
    array = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    flat = array.reshape(-1, order="F") if array.ndim == 2 else array.reshape(-1)
    parts = []
    for value in flat:
        value = float(value)
        parts.append("NA" if math.isnan(value) else format(value, ".16g"))
    return " ".join(parts)

x = Zoo([1.0, 3.0, 5.0], [1.0, 2.0, 4.0])
y = Zoo([2.0, 4.0, 6.0], [2.0, 3.0, 4.0])
z = cbind_zoo(x, y, all=False)
print(show(z.data))
print(show(z.index))
